run.researchNotes: Sector-only run: 34 web searches plus 1 page fetch. companies array left empty and top3 omitted as instructed. Macro is as at 16 Nov 2026: CPI Oct 2026 (6.09%) from MoSPI; repo 5.50% from MPC 7 Oct 2026; GDP Q1 FY27 7.8%; non-food credit 19.1% (30 Sep 2026); OBICUS Q1 FY27 CU 74.6%. Rupee: no FBIL reference rate or PTI close for 12/13 Nov 2026 was found; 93.70 is the PTI provisional close of 11 Nov 2026. Bank ratings use Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026) results; valuation multiples for SBI, BoB, PNB, Canara, Union, Indian Bank, BoI and BoM are from a single 26 Aug 2026 table (Sahi, citing exchange data) so they are 11 weeks old; IOB, UCO, Central and PSB multiples come from separate data pages and differ by source (IOB 1.80x vs 2.13x). Competition table could only be built at bank-group level (PSB 54.4% / private 40.6%, Dec 2025); bank-level advance shares for one common period were not found for 8 players, so players are groups. SAM could not be sized on a method distinct from TAM and is null. Budget block covers recapitalisation (FY22-FY27), MISS and the MSE credit guarantee head; Actuals for FY24-FY25 and RE for MISS were not found. Global CAGR (15/10/5/3y), growth forecast and peer 5y return/forward PE were not established and are null. Conflicts: FY26 remittances $110.47bn (workers' remittances) vs $144.79bn (net private transfers incl. NRI deposits); Nifty PSU Bank P/B 1.17 (Screener, 3 Aug 2026) vs 1.20 (Sharpely, undated) vs ~1.58 (press, earlier 2026 peak); PSB share of SCB loans 54.4% vs PSB gross advances/TAM 59.7% (different bases - gross incl. overseas vs domestic). Top-up, 16 Nov 2026, 12 further searches. Competition rebuilt on one metric and one date: each bank's reported advances at 31 Mar 2026 divided by RBI SCB bank credit of Rs 2,13,61,435 cr at 31 Mar 2026; eleven named banks cover 82.5%. Caveat: bank figures are global/gross advances (SBI, BoB, PNB, Canara, BoI, Indian Bank include overseas books; Kotak is net) while the RBI total is domestic, so named shares are modestly overstated and the residual understated. Bank of India: Rs 7.71 lakh cr gross (management call) used over Rs 7,40,314 cr (JM Financial, likely net). TAM corrected: the earlier 21,290,000 was non-food credit; total bank credit at 31 Mar 2026 is 21,361,435 (RBI). SAM set to non-food credit, excluding food credit (FCI/state procurement consortium lending allocated outside competitive markets). Global growth: no source found on McKinsey's revenue basis for 15y, 10y, 5y or 3y CAGR; y5 given is IBISWorld's Global Commercial Banks revenue CAGR 2020-2025 (4.3%); MarketLine puts global bank ASSETS CAGR 2020-2025 at 5.0%; y15, y10 and y3 not found and omitted. Forecast: only consultancy forecasts found; TechSci's commercial-banking market forecast of 11.47% CAGR 2025-2031 is used but is on a narrower market definition ($3.2tn in 2025) and runs well above the 4-5% historical rates, so treat it as an outlier. The three bank-GROUP rows sent earlier (Public sector banks 54.4, Private sector banks 40.6, Foreign/SFB/other 5.0, Dec 2025) are on a different metric and period and should be dropped from competition.players; they do not match these bank names, so a merge by name would keep them. Top-up 2, 16 Nov 2026, 2 further searches. global.cagr y15, y10 and y3: McKinsey's archive (2014-2022 reviews) and the 2026 review were searched for a banking-revenue series on the 2025 basis ($6.4tn revenues before risk costs). None was found that gives a 2010, 2015 or 2022 figure on that basis. The only 2023 figure found ($6.8tn) is total revenue from global financial intermediation, which is a wider measure than bank revenue, so a 3-year CAGR would mix bases. All three keys are omitted. competition.players restated on one measure and one period: reported advances divided by RBI scheduled commercial bank credit of Rs 2,13,61,435 cr, 31 Mar 2026. The residual row is restated on that basis. The 'Public sector banks (12)' row is restated from the Finance Ministry aggregate of PSB gross advances, Rs 127 lakh cr at 31 Mar 2026 (59.45%). That aggregate includes overseas books, so it overstates the domestic share; the Dec 2025 domestic loan share was 54.4%. It is a group total that overlaps the individual PSB rows, so it must not be added to them. 'Private sector banks' and 'Foreign, small finance and other scheduled banks' could not be restated: no aggregate advances figure for 31 Mar 2026 was found for either group. They are Dec 2025 group rows on a different measure that overlap the named banks, and should be deleted from competition.players. A by-name merge cannot remove them. Top-up 3, 16 Nov 2026, 2 further searches. competition.players: every row is now restated on one measure, share of scheduled commercial bank credit, and one date, end-March 2026 (31 Mar 2026). The three bank-GROUP rows replace their Dec 2025 values with RBI's Annual BSR-1 March 2026 (released 29 May 2026): PSBs 52.9%, private banks 39.4%, others 7.7% (residual). This also supersedes the 59.45% PSB figure in top-up 2, which was gross advances including overseas books. The eleven bank rows are each bank's reported advances at 31 Mar 2026 divided by RBI Section-42 SCB bank credit of Rs 2,13,61,435 cr. Most use global or gross advances and so are modestly overstated against the domestic BSR group shares; for example, the named PSBs sum to above their group's share once overseas books are counted. Group rows are totals that overlap the bank rows; read them separately and do not add them to the bank rows. global.cagr y15, y10 and y3 remain unestablished. McKinsey gives banking revenue of $1.8tn in 2000 and $6.5tn in 2024 (5.4% CAGR over 24 years) and 4.6% for 2023-24. However, its 2026 review restates 2024 at $6.1tn, so the series is not consistent. No published 2010, 2015 or 2022 value on the 2025 basis ($6.4tn) was found. A 15-, 10- or 3-year CAGR would therefore mix bases, so these keys are omitted.

industryMap.structure: 12 listed public sector banks held 54.4% of scheduled commercial bank loans at Dec 2025 against 40.6% for private banks; SBI alone holds ~20% of net advances.
industryMap.valueChain: Deposit gathering -> capital and wholesale funding -> credit origination -> technology and digital rails -> recovery/resolution -> third-party distribution; second-order beneficiaries are core-banking vendors (Infosys, TCS, Nucleus, Intellect), rating agencies (CRISIL, ICRA, CARE) and bank-owned insurers/AMCs (SBI Life, SBI Card, Canara Robeco).
industryMap.tam: Scheduled commercial bank credit of Rs 212.9 lakh crore at end-FY26 (RBI data via Sahi), grown 15.9% in FY26.
industryMap.policy: Post-clean-up era: no recapitalisation since FY22; ECL provisioning from 1 Apr 2027; minimum public shareholding deadline of 1 Aug 2026 for IOB, UCO, Central and PSB; a further PSB consolidation round under discussion.
industryMap.geopolitics: Banking is domestically funded; external exposure runs through remittances (FY26 net private transfers $144.79bn), FDI and an Iran-war oil shock that pushed the rupee to ~94-95/$ and CPI above 6%.

exclusions.reason: RBI classifies IDBI Bank as a private sector bank since 2019 and the government stake is under strategic sale; it is not one of the 12 public sector banks.

global.indiaPosition: India's banks earn roughly 3% of global bank profits from an economy that is growing 7-8% in real terms, which is why Indian bank credit is compounding near 19% while global banking revenues grew about 5% in 2025. The public sector banks are the main vehicle of that growth: they held 54.4% of Indian bank loans at Dec 2025 and their share is rising, not falling. Only SBI ranks in the global top 50 by assets (43rd), so the scale gap with Chinese, US and European banks remains large. That gap is the stated rationale for the government's next consolidation round.

policyEvolution.what: Nationalisation of 14 banks (1969) and 6 more (1980); directed credit, priority-sector lending and administered rates made PSBs the instrument of credit policy.
Narasimham Committee I (1991) and II (1998): CRR/SLR cuts, income recognition and NPA norms, Basel I capital, entry of new private banks from 1993, and partial PSB listings.
SARFAESI Act 2002 for secured recovery; Basel II/III; the 2004-2011 infrastructure credit boom whose bad loans were later evergreened through restructuring.

RBI Asset Quality Review (2015) forced NPA recognition; Indradhanush (2015), IBC (2016), recapitalisation bonds (Rs 2.76 lakh cr of Rs 3.11 lakh cr infused FY17-FY21), PCA, and mergers that cut PSBs from 27 to 12.

Last recapitalisation in FY22 (Rs 20,000 cr); EASE reforms; record PSB profit of Rs 1.98 lakh cr in FY26 with multi-decadal-low NPAs; ECL directions issued 27 Apr 2026, effective 1 Apr 2027; MPS deadline 1 Aug 2026; next consolidation round debated.

regulation.regulator: Reserve Bank of India (prudential and monetary), with the Ministry of Finance - DFS as owner of PSBs and SEBI for listing and public-shareholding rules
regulation.rules: Banking Regulation Act 1949 and the Bank Nationalisation Acts of 1970/1980; Basel III capital (system CRAR 17.2% at Sep 2025); priority-sector lending targets; the new Commercial Banks - Asset Classification, Provisioning and Income Recognition Directions 2026 introducing three-stage ECL from 1 Apr 2027 while retaining NPA classification; FDI in PSBs capped at 20%.
regulation.underReview: ECL transition (loans fair-valued on 1 Apr 2027, transition period to 31 Mar 2031); PSB consolidation; MPS compliance for four PSBs; policy stance moved to calibrated tightening on 7 Oct 2026 with the next MPC on 2-4 Dec 2026.
regulation.costOfChange: ICRA expects the ECL impact on capitalisation to be moderate, but Vinod Kothari expects it to hurt bank profits and retained earnings in FY28; RBI rejected requests for more time and PSB stocks fell up to 2.5% on 28 Apr 2026. Bank-level day-one ECL estimates were not found.

geopolitics.importDependence: Banking imports almost nothing physical; the dependence is on imported core-banking and cloud technology and on oil-driven inflation. The 2026 Iran war oil shock lifted CPI to 6.09% and forced a 25bp repo hike, which raises deposit costs.
geopolitics.exportExposure: Exposure runs through overseas branches (SBI foreign-office advances +20.01% in FY26) and remittance flows; FY26 net private transfers were $144.79bn per RBI.
geopolitics.tariffRisk: Indirect: US tariff threats on countries buying Russian oil (Jan 2026) and a weaker rupee (~94/$) hit export-oriented borrowers, not banks directly.
geopolitics.sanctionRisk: Low for domestic PSBs; overseas branches must comply with US/EU sanctions on counterparties tied to Iran and Russia.
geopolitics.concentration: Remittance sources are concentrated: the US (27.7%) and UAE (19.2%) supplied ~47% of FY24 inward remittances; the GCC share fell to 38% from ~47% in FY17.

industry.structure: India has 12 public sector banks, led by SBI with about a fifth of system advances, followed by a mid-tier of Bank of Baroda, PNB, Canara and Union, a second tier of Indian Bank and Bank of India, and four small banks (Central, IOB, UCO, PSB) plus Bank of Maharashtra. PSBs held 54.4% of bank loans at Dec 2025, up from 53.11% a year earlier, as their loan growth of 18-28% outran private banks' low-to-mid teens. The government owns a majority of every PSB, from just over half at SBI to about 93% at Punjab & Sind Bank, which shapes capital raising, pay, merger decisions and float. PSBs earned a record Rs 1.98 lakh cr in FY26, up 11%.
industry.cyclePosition: Late expansion. Non-food credit is growing 19.1%, GNPA is at multi-decadal lows and credit costs are near cycle troughs (SBI 0.22% in Q2 FY27), which is where earnings peak. The rate cycle turned with the 7 Oct 2026 hike and CPI above 6%, and ECL lands on 1 Apr 2027, so provisions are more likely to rise than fall from here. Loan growth running well ahead of deposit growth across PSBs is the classic late-cycle signal.
industry.profitPool: SCB profit after tax rose to Rs 4,05,268 cr in FY26 (RBI FSR, Jun 2026), of which PSBs earned about Rs 1.98 lakh cr, roughly 49%. The pool is moving toward PSBs: Q2 FY27 PSB PAT grew ~27% YoY vs ~24% for private banks (MOFSL), and PSB NIMs held while private-bank NIMs fell 8-20bp. Within PSBs, SBI earned about 40% of group profit in Q3 FY26. Part of the Q2 FY27 gain was treasury and one-off income (BoB treasury Rs 4,093 cr; SBI stake-sale gain), which will not recur at this level.
industry.technologyShift: Distribution is now almost entirely digital: 98.8% of SBI transactions ran through alternate channels in Q1 FY27. PSBs are moving MSME underwriting to digital-footprint models (Rs 41,500 cr sanctioned in eight months of 2025). Globally, agentic AI, fintechs and stablecoins (>$300bn) are eroding customer stickiness, and ECL demands PD/LGD/EAD models with forward-looking macro inputs that most PSBs are still building.

Supports NRI and household deposit inflows, which PSB branch networks capture

valueChain.name: 1. Deposit gathering (households, CASA, NRI)
valueChain.what: Branch and digital mobilisation of retail and NRI deposits, the cheapest funding in the system

valueChain.name: 2. Capital and wholesale funding
valueChain.what: QIPs, government OFS, AT1/Tier II bonds and certificates of deposit to fund loan growth above deposit growth

valueChain.name: 3. Credit origination (RAM and corporate)
valueChain.what: Retail, agriculture, MSME and corporate lending; RAM grew 15-21% at large PSBs in Q1 FY27

valueChain.name: 4. Technology and digital rails
valueChain.what: Core banking, digital lending journeys, ECL modelling and risk systems

valueChain.name: 5. Recovery and resolution
valueChain.what: Recoveries from written-off and NPA accounts via IBC, SARFAESI and ARCs; NPA recovery rate 26.2% in FY25

valueChain.name: 6. Third-party distribution and subsidiaries
valueChain.what: Insurance, mutual funds and cards sold through PSB branches and housed in listed subsidiaries

valueChain.name: 7. End users
valueChain.what: Households, farmers, MSMEs and corporates borrowing and saving with PSBs

competition.concentration: Highly concentrated at the top: the three largest banks (SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank) held 44% of advances and 43% of deposits at Mar 2026; SBI alone ~20% of net advances.
competition.entryBarriers: Banking licence, minimum capital, deposit franchise, branch network and trust; no new universal bank of PSB scale has been licensed in recent years (INFERENCE).
competition.substitution: NBFCs, co-lending, corporate bonds, commercial paper, ECBs and private credit substitute for bank loans to large borrowers; fintech payments and stablecoins compete for transaction balances.
competition.pricingBehaviour: Rational: repo-linked (EBLR) pricing transmits policy moves; the binding competition is now on deposits, where PSBs' CASA ratios are slipping and term-deposit rates are being bid up.
competition.metric: share of scheduled commercial bank credit (each bank's reported advances / RBI total bank credit)

monitorables: Deposit growth vs loan growth: the thesis needs PSB deposit growth back above ~13% while loans run 15-19%; CD ratios above 88% (Union 88.13% today) would break it.
CASA ratios: further declines like Canara's 28.5% to 26.4% would compress NIM once EBLR repricing is absorbed.
Day-one ECL impact disclosures ahead of 1 Apr 2027 and the hit to CET1 at each bank.
Agriculture GNPA (6.0% at Sep 2025, 36.3% of all GNPA) as ECL and food inflation bite.
RBI MPC 2-4 Dec 2026: another hike raises deposit costs and bond losses; a pause supports margins.
MPS OFS supply in IOB, UCO, Central and PSB, and any formal merger announcement (e.g. Canara-Union).
Treasury/one-off share of PSB profits: Q2 FY27 was flattered by BoB's Rs 4,093 cr treasury gain and SBI's stake sale.

glossary.meaning: Net interest margin: interest earned minus interest paid, as a percentage of interest-earning assets.
Current and savings account deposits, the cheapest funding; the CASA ratio is their share of total deposits.
Gross and net non-performing assets: loans overdue 90+ days, before and after provisions, as % of advances.
Provision coverage ratio: provisions held against NPAs as % of gross NPAs.
Credit-to-deposit ratio: advances as % of deposits; high values signal funding strain.
New loans turning NPA in a period as % of standard advances at the start.
Loan-loss provisions charged in a period as % of average advances.
Capital to risk-weighted assets ratio; CET1 is its core equity component.
Expected credit loss: forward-looking three-stage provisioning replacing incurred-loss rules for Indian banks from 1 Apr 2027.
Retail, agriculture and MSME loans, PSBs' core growth segment.
External benchmark lending rate, usually the repo rate, to which floating loans reset.
Minimum public shareholding (25%), offer for sale by the government, and qualified institutional placement of new shares.
Pre-provision operating profit: net total income minus operating expenses, before provisions and tax.
